title: Sociodemographic Bias in Language Models: A Survey and Forward Path

bias_targets.methodology: Surveyed a wide range of intrinsic and extrinsic measurement approaches, including distance-based metrics (e.g., WEAT, ECT), probing classifiers on latent spaces, performance-based metrics (e.g., true positive rates across groups), and prompt-based metrics (templates, counterfactuals, and sentence masking).
Surveyed literature utilizing distance-based vector space metrics, probing, and extrinsic prompt-based evaluations to quantify racial disparities in model representations and downstream tasks.
Reviewed methods spanning vector space similarities, prompt-based template generation, and variance of normalized probabilities across demographic groups using masked language models.
Surveyed studies using prompt-based methods and representational evaluations to measure biases against different nationalities in natural language generation and embedding spaces.
Surveyed methods such as template-based prompts and counterfactual dataset substitution to measure anti-LGBTQ+ and sexual orientation biases in language models.
Surveyed metrics quantifying representational harms and differential performance in language models regarding people with disabilities.
Surveyed intrinsic and extrinsic evaluation methodologies assessing differential model performance and representation based on age.
Included in the survey's taxonomy of sociodemographic biases, reviewing overarching intrinsic and extrinsic metrics applied to political leanings.
Included in the survey's taxonomy, evaluating how representational and allocative harms are measured regarding physical appearance.
Included in the survey's taxonomy of sociodemographic biases, surveying general distance, probing, and prompt-based measurement techniques.
